prompt: What does PortFast do on an end-device access port?
options: It makes the port a root port so user traffic avoids the normal tree.
It filters all BPDUs so the host can never influence the bridge election.
It permits immediate forwarding while spanning tree remains active.
It waits for a PC's agreement BPDU before skipping the learning state.
explanation: PortFast lets an edge port forward immediately. STP keeps running, and a received BPDU removes the operational edge status.

whyWrong.0: PortFast does not make the port a root port.
whyWrong.1: Filtering BPDUs is a separate feature.
whyWrong.3: End hosts take no part in a proposal and agreement handshake.

prompt: Which global command enables PortFast on nontrunking ports of a 2960-style switch?
options: spanning-tree bpduguard enable
spanning-tree portfast default
spanning-tree guard root
spanning-tree portfast trunk
explanation: spanning-tree portfast default enables PortFast on all nontrunking access ports. A trunk needs the interface form, spanning-tree portfast trunk.

whyWrong.0: That enables BPDU guard on an interface, not PortFast.
whyWrong.2: Root guard protects a boundary and does not create an edge port.
whyWrong.3: That is an interface command for PortFast on a trunk.

prompt: What triggers loop guard on a root port that was receiving BPDUs?
options: Expected BPDU information expires while the physical link remains up.
The port receives its first BPDU while operational PortFast is enabled.
The local switch learns a host MAC address on the root interface.
The peer advertises a lower root BID while continuing normal BPDU exchange.
explanation: Loop guard reacts when expected BPDUs stop arriving while the link stays up. It stops the port from going designated and forwarding.

whyWrong.1: An unexpected BPDU on an edge port is the BPDU guard case.
whyWrong.2: MAC learning does not trigger loop guard.
whyWrong.3: A superior BPDU is the root guard case.

prompt: How do the global and interface BPDU filter differ?
options: The global PortFast form withdraws filtering after a BPDU; the interface form suppresses BPDUs independently.
The global form filters user broadcasts; the interface form filters user multicast without affecting STP.
The global form applies only to trunks; the interface form applies only to nontrunking access ports.
The global form err-disables after a BPDU; the interface form waits for a superior root advertisement.
explanation: The global filter, which applies to PortFast ports, stops filtering when a BPDU arrives. The interface filter always suppresses BPDUs.

whyWrong.1: BPDU filter affects BPDUs, not user broadcasts or multicasts.
whyWrong.2: The global form follows PortFast status, and the interface form is not limited that way.
whyWrong.3: Those describe guard actions, not filtering.

prompt: How does root guard differ from BPDU guard?
options: Root guard rejects every BPDU; BPDU guard rejects only a lower-priority root.
Root guard rejects superior information; BPDU guard reacts to any received BPDU.
Root guard detects BPDU silence; BPDU guard detects changes in interface speed.
Root guard uses errdisable; BPDU guard uses a per-VLAN root-inconsistent state.
explanation: Root guard reacts only to superior BPDUs. BPDU guard reacts to any BPDU.

whyWrong.0: The triggers are reversed.
whyWrong.2: Missing BPDUs are the loop guard case, and speed changes are unrelated.
whyWrong.3: The states are reversed: root guard uses root inconsistency and BPDU guard uses errdisable.

prompt: With no errdisable recovery timer, which two states clear automatically once their cause ends? (Choose two.)
options: Administrative shutdown after the peer link becomes healthy.
Loop inconsistency after expected BPDUs resume.
An administratively disabled SVI after the correct VLAN is created.
Root inconsistency after superior information ceases.
BPDU-guard errdisable after the switch stops sending BPDUs.
explanation: Root-inconsistent and loop-inconsistent ports recover automatically when their trigger stops. BPDU-guard errdisable needs manual recovery or an enabled recovery timer.

whyWrong.0: A configured shutdown stays until someone removes it.
whyWrong.2: Creating a VLAN does not remove a shutdown on an SVI.
whyWrong.4: Without errdisable recovery, the port stays err-disabled.

prompt: A root-facing point-to-point uplink needs loop guard and a downstream boundary needs root guard. What is the principle?
options: Choose the guard by the intended role; root and loop guard cannot coexist on one interface.
Use root guard on every root port because its name identifies where it belongs.
Install both guards on each uplink so either a received or missing BPDU is covered.
Use loop guard on PC access ports because their lack of BPDUs needs protection.
explanation: Pick the guard for the port's role: root guard on designated boundary ports, loop guard on root and alternate ports. Root guard and loop guard cannot be used together on one interface.

whyWrong.1: A root port must accept superior BPDUs, which root guard would reject.
whyWrong.2: The two guards are mutually exclusive on one interface.
whyWrong.3: Edge ports normally send no BPDUs, so loop guard does not apply.

prompt: What caused the Fa0/5 outage, and how do you recover?
options: The port is a normal alternate; remove the redundant uplink to make it designated.
A BPDU arrived on the guarded port; remove its source, then shut/no-shut the port.
Expected BPDUs stopped arriving; lower the recovery interval to force learning.
A better root was received; raise SW1's bridge priority to clear the state.
explanation: The log names BPDU guard and the port is err-disabled. Remove the BPDU source, then shut and no shut the port.

whyWrong.0: Err-disabled is not a normal alternate state.
whyWrong.2: Missing BPDUs are the loop guard case.
whyWrong.3: A better root BPDU is the root guard case.

exhibit.title: SW1 representative evidence
exhibit.text:
Fa0/5   err-disabled   10
%PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Fa0/5, putting Fa0/5 in err-disable state

prompt: VLAN 20 is blocked on Gi1/0/10 while another VLAN on the trunk works. What is the diagnosis?
options: Loop guard detected missing expected BPDUs from the intended root neighbor.
BPDU guard disabled the entire physical interface after receiving a BPDU.
Root guard received superior information for VLAN 20 and blocked that instance.
PortFast suppressed the interface's BPDUs until a recovery timer expires.
explanation: The port shows root inconsistency, so root guard received superior information. In Rapid PVST+ it blocks only VLAN 20's instance.

whyWrong.0: Loop inconsistency is triggered by missing BPDUs.
whyWrong.1: BPDU guard err-disables the whole interface.
whyWrong.3: PortFast does not suppress BPDUs.

prompt: Which two statements about recovery from a BPDU-guard violation are correct? (Choose two.)
options: The source should be corrected before the interface is re-enabled.
Changing the recovery interval alone enables recovery for BPDU guard.
An enabled recovery timer can retry the port but cannot remove the BPDU source.
Root-inconsistent recovery must be enabled before errdisable can clear.
A single received inferior BPDU cannot cause another violation after recovery.
explanation: Remove the BPDU source before re-enabling the port. A recovery timer retries the port but does not remove the source, so the violation repeats if the BPDU source remains.

whyWrong.1: The cause itself must also be enabled for recovery.
whyWrong.3: Root inconsistency is a different state and clears by itself.
whyWrong.4: BPDU guard reacts to any received BPDU.

prompt: CORE must stay the root. A training switch attaches to ASW1 Gi0/2, a designated port. Where do you apply root guard?
options: On ASW1 Gi0/2, where superior information could enter from the training switch.
On the training switch's own uplink, where its lower-priority BID originates.
On every designated CORE port, including unrelated campus boundaries.
On ASW1's uplink toward CORE, where the best root information is received.
explanation: Put root guard on ASW1 Gi0/2, the designated port facing the switch that must not become root. It blocks superior BPDUs from entering there.

whyWrong.1: Root guard must be on the switch you control.
whyWrong.2: A blanket CORE policy affects unrelated links.
whyWrong.3: That is the legitimate path to the root, so root guard would break it.

prompt: Fa0/7 is an operational access port with no interface overrides. What happens when a switch sending BPDUs is attached, given the global configuration shown?
options: The port remains unprotected because no interface-specific guard line exists.
The port enters root inconsistency only if the attached bridge has a lower BID.
The operational PortFast port is covered by BPDU guard and becomes err-disabled.
The port silently filters the received BPDU and remains an operational edge.
explanation: The global PortFast and BPDU guard defaults cover this operational PortFast port. A received BPDU err-disables it.

whyWrong.0: Global defaults apply without per-interface commands.
whyWrong.1: BPDU guard reacts to any BPDU, not just superior ones.
whyWrong.3: No BPDU filter is configured.

exhibit.title: SW1 running-config excerpt
exhibit.text:
spanning-tree portfast default
spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default
interface FastEthernet0/7
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10

prompt: A trunk to a server without PortFast must be err-disabled on any received BPDU. Which interface command does that?
options: spanning-tree portfast trunk
spanning-tree guard root
spanning-tree loopguard default
spanning-tree bpduguard enable
explanation: spanning-tree bpduguard enable on an interface works with or without PortFast. It err-disables the port on any BPDU.

whyWrong.0: PortFast does not err-disable on BPDUs.
whyWrong.1: Root guard reacts only to superior BPDUs.
whyWrong.2: That is a global loop guard command.

prompt: SW3 Gi0/2 was a root port that received BPDUs. What do these observations show?
options: The interface was disabled by BPDU guard, so every VLAN must be physically down.
Expected BPDUs stopped arriving; the output does not by itself prove the physical cause.
The fiber receive strand is conclusively broken because the port is still connected.
A newly received priority-zero BPDU forced SW3 to reject a superior root bridge.
explanation: Loop inconsistency means expected BPDUs stopped arriving while the link stayed up. The output does not show why they stopped.

whyWrong.0: The state is loop inconsistency, not BPDU guard errdisable.
whyWrong.2: Other causes, such as a filter, give the same symptom.
whyWrong.3: A superior BPDU is the root guard case.

exhibit.title: SW3 representative observations
exhibit.text:
Gi0/2 physical status: connected
VLAN0010  GigabitEthernet0/2  Loop Inconsistent
VLAN0020  GigabitEthernet0/2  Loop Inconsistent
Received BPDU counter stopped increasing before the event.

prompt: A host-port template should detect unexpected BPDUs. What is wrong with it?
options: Replace BPDU guard with root guard so every BPDU still produces the required errdisable.
Keep the template because interface filtering restores guard visibility after the first BPDU.
Remove PortFast but retain filtering so BPDU guard can inspect normal transit BPDUs.
Remove interface filtering so the intended policy can process received BPDUs.
explanation: The interface BPDU filter drops received BPDUs before BPDU guard sees them, so the port never err-disables. Remove the filter and keep PortFast and BPDU guard.

whyWrong.0: Root guard reacts only to superior BPDUs and does not err-disable.
whyWrong.1: The fallback behavior belongs to the global filter, not the interface filter.
whyWrong.2: Removing PortFast does not remove the filter.

exhibit.title: SW1 host-port configuration
exhibit.text:
interface FastEthernet0/5
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 10
 spanning-tree portfast
 spanning-tree bpduguard enable
 spanning-tree bpdufilter enable

prompt: A port is err-disabled by BPDU guard and the BPDU source is gone. What does the recovery configuration show?
options: The port will be retried after 60 seconds because every cause inherits the interval.
The port must stay disabled until the interval is restored to the default 300 seconds.
The interval is 60 seconds, but BPDU-guard automatic recovery remains disabled.
The port is now root-inconsistent and will recover when a superior BPDU expires.
explanation: The interval is 60 seconds, but BPDU-guard recovery is not enabled. Recover the port manually or enable recovery for bpduguard.

whyWrong.0: The interval does not enable recovery for every cause.
whyWrong.1: The default interval is not a prerequisite for recovery.
whyWrong.3: Changing a timer does not change the protection state.

exhibit.title: SW1# show errdisable recovery — abbreviated
exhibit.text:
ErrDisable Reason             Timer Status
bpduguard                     Disabled
Timer interval: 60 seconds

exhibit.title: Supplied protection evidence
exhibit.text:
Fa0/8 is an access port.
Configured: spanning-tree portfast
No BPDU guard or BPDU filter at interface or global scope.
After a BPDU arrives: operational edge false; interface remains connected.

prompt: A received BPDU turns an RSTP port from edge to non-edge. What explains the configuration and state?
options: The received BPDU is discarded because PortFast disables spanning-tree processing.
The port must be err-disabled because every configured PortFast port has BPDU guard.
The switch must have erased the PortFast command when the first BPDU arrived.
PortFast can remain configured even though the port no longer operates as an edge.
explanation: Configured PortFast and operational edge status are separate. A BPDU removes edge status, but the PortFast command stays.

whyWrong.0: PortFast does not turn off BPDU processing.
whyWrong.1: PortFast does not include BPDU guard.

exhibit.title: Supplied protection evidence
exhibit.text:
Global: spanning-tree portfast default
Global: spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default
Gi0/1: operational trunk; operational PortFast false
No interface BPDU-guard enable or other overrides.

prompt: A server trunk must reject every BPDU. Why does the global guard not protect it?
options: Global BPDU guard suppresses sent BPDUs but never processes received BPDUs.
The root priority must first be lower than the server’s priority before the guard applies.
The trunk is not operationally PortFast, so it is outside this global guard scope.
Global defaults apply only when every VLAN elects this switch as root.
explanation: The global BPDU guard covers only operational PortFast ports. This trunk is not one, so configure BPDU guard on the interface.

whyWrong.0: BPDU guard acts on received BPDUs, not sent ones.
whyWrong.1: BPDU guard does not depend on priority.
whyWrong.3: Root identity does not matter for the global default.

exhibit.title: Supplied protection evidence
exhibit.text:
Gi1/0/7: err-disabled
No log cause has yet been collected.
The switch has several different interface security features configured.

prompt: What do you check before choosing how to recover an err-disabled port?
options: The configured VLAN root priority, which identifies every errdisable cause.
The log reason for the affected interface and its relevant configuration.
The lowest MAC address in the switch’s forwarding table.
The STP alternate-port count, which proves BPDU guard caused the outage.
explanation: Errdisable is a state with several possible causes. Read the log reason and the interface configuration to find which feature triggered it.

whyWrong.0: Bridge priority does not identify errdisable causes.
whyWrong.2: A learned MAC does not show why the port was disabled.
whyWrong.3: An alternate port is a normal state and does not prove BPDU guard.

exhibit.title: Supplied protection evidence
exhibit.text:
Only links: CORE—ACCESS—LAB. All carry VLAN 10.
Required root: CORE priority 24576. ACCESS priority 32768. LAB priority 32768.
ACCESS Gi0/1 faces CORE; Gi0/2 faces LAB.
Gi0/1 config: spanning-tree guard root; state Root Inconsistent.
Gi0/2 config: no guard; intended designated boundary.
No other root source or physical failure is present.

prompt: Which fix keeps the root boundary and restores the legitimate upstream path?
options: Move both root guard and loop guard to the lab-facing port as one combined policy.
Lower ACCESS’s priority below CORE so its root-facing uplink no longer receives superior information.
Remove root guard from the CORE-facing uplink and place it on the designated LAB-facing boundary.
Disable spanning tree on the uplink and leave both guards in their current places.
explanation: Root guard blocked the legitimate path to CORE. Move it to the designated LAB-facing port and use loop guard on the uplink if needed.

whyWrong.0: Root guard and loop guard cannot coexist on one interface.
whyWrong.1: Making ACCESS the root breaks the design.
whyWrong.3: Disabling STP does not fix guard placement.

exhibit.title: Supplied protection evidence
exhibit.text:
Port policy: access host edge, interface BPDU guard enabled.
Recovery: bpduguard Enabled; interval 60 seconds.
Observed sequence repeated twice: recovery attempts re-enable Fa0/5; a new received-BPDU log appears; Fa0/5 becomes err-disabled again.
Cable audit: a BPDU-sending switch remains attached.

prompt: A host port keeps going down repeatedly after timed recovery. What explains it?
options: Timed recovery is disabled because the interval is shorter than the default 300 seconds.
Timed recovery is working, but the continuing BPDU source immediately violates the policy again.
Root guard is moving the root bridge at each retry, causing the host’s periodic loss.
The first successful retry proves the BPDU source is gone and later events are stale.
explanation: Timed recovery works, but the BPDU source is still attached. Each retry gets another BPDU and BPDU guard errdisables the port again. Remove the source.

whyWrong.0: The cause is enabled and a 60-second interval is valid.
whyWrong.2: The event is BPDU guard, not a root election.
whyWrong.3: Each new event shows the source is still there.

exhibit.title: Supplied protection evidence
exhibit.text:
Gi0/1: root-facing point-to-point port; BPDUs received before the incident; physical connected; VLAN 10 Loop Inconsistent.
Fa0/8: host port; physical status err-disabled; log names bpduguard.
No automatic errdisable recovery configured.

prompt: Fa0/8 shows a BPDU-guard event and Gi0/1 shows loop inconsistency. Which two actions fit? (Choose two.)
options: Remove Fa0/8’s BPDU source, then recover that err-disabled interface.
Lower the root priority to resolve both incidents without changing either connection.
Bounce Gi0/1 repeatedly so it forwards without receiving new BPDUs.
Treat both ports as physically disconnected and replace both cables immediately.
Inspect BPDU delivery/filtering toward Gi0/1 while retaining its loop guard.
explanation: Fa0/8 needs its BPDU source removed and then recovery. Gi0/1 lost expected BPDUs, so check BPDU delivery and filtering toward it and keep loop guard on.

whyWrong.2: Bouncing the port does not restore BPDU delivery.
whyWrong.3: Nothing shows two cable failures.

prompt: What is the default errdisable recovery interval on the IOS platforms in this chapter?
options: 30 seconds
60 seconds
300 seconds
600 seconds
explanation: The default interval is 300 seconds. Recovery for a cause must still be enabled separately.

whyWrong.0: 30 seconds is not the default.
whyWrong.1: 60 seconds is a common configured value, not the default.
whyWrong.3: 600 seconds is not the default.

prompt: What does BPDU guard do when a BPDU arrives on a protected port?
options: It blocks only the VLAN that sent the BPDU.
It puts the whole port in the err-disabled state.
It drops the BPDU and keeps forwarding.
It makes the port the root port.
explanation: BPDU guard err-disables the whole port. Root and loop inconsistency block only one VLAN's instance.

whyWrong.0: That describes root guard or loop guard behavior in Rapid PVST+.
whyWrong.2: Dropping BPDUs is what BPDU filter does.
whyWrong.3: BPDU guard does not change port roles.

prompt: Which global command enables BPDU guard on PortFast ports?
options: spanning-tree guard root
spanning-tree loopguard default
spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default
spanning-tree bpdufilter enable
explanation: spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default turns on BPDU guard for operational PortFast ports.

whyWrong.0: That is the root guard interface command.
whyWrong.3: That is an interface BPDU filter command.

prompt: On which ports is loop guard intended to run?
options: Edge ports facing hosts
Designated ports facing a new switch
Root and alternate ports on point-to-point links
Any port that has PortFast enabled
explanation: Loop guard protects root and alternate ports from BPDU loss. Root guard goes on designated boundary ports.

whyWrong.0: Edge ports normally send no BPDUs, so loop guard does not apply.
whyWrong.1: Designated boundary ports are where root guard goes.
whyWrong.3: PortFast ports are edge ports.
